primitives.name: Ball Detection Pipeline
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Pipeline: YOLOv4 ball/person detection → Kalman filter/smoother tracking → OpenPose head centers → fixed head-height thresholds defining "risk regions" (15% and other levels) → binary high/low-risk label per tackle.

primitives.assumptions: Fixed ball detector trained on 551 images; assumes consistent broadcast video quality.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when video lacks clear ball visibility or exceeds training domain.

primitives.name: Head Height Thresholding
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Pipeline: YOLOv4 ball/person detection → Kalman filter/smoother tracking → OpenPose head centers → fixed head-height thresholds defining "risk regions" (15% and other levels) → binary high/low-risk label per tackle.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H_{head}': 'height of head center above ground (meters)', 'R_{risk}': 'fixed threshold height (meters)', 'L_{risk}': 'binary label {0,1} indicating risk'}
primitives.assumptions: Injury risk correlates with head position relative to fixed height zones; assumes static risk thresholds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Invalid when head tracking fails or thresholds misalign with actual injury mechanics.

layer2.mapping: Maps 3D head positions to scalar risk scores using fixed thresholds, equivalent to a step function in height space.

primitives.assumptions: Heuristic labels approximate true injury risk; no real-world injury outcomes used for training.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ineffective when heuristic does not reflect real injury patterns.

layer2.mapping: Combines ball and head tracking into a single binary risk classifier using fixed thresholds.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology combines object detection (YOLOv4), motion tracking (Kalman filters), and pose estimation (OpenPose) to infer tackle risk. The system operates under a fixed-height threshold model for head positioning, which acts as a proxy for injury likelihood. This approach fails due to high processing failure rates (41%), reliance on manual tuning, and lack of real injury data. The pipeline's modular structure allows for component-wise failure but lacks robustness against variability in video input or injury dynamics. The binary classification task is inherently limited by the heuristic nature of the risk label, leading to poor inter-rater reliability (κ=0.28). The system cannot generalize beyond its training domain and exhibits strong leakage from video quality and scene complexity.
